_readme: SPOKEN help for the Settings panel — the words the app says when you arm the '?'
button and then tap a control, a label, or a tab.
THIS FILE IS NOT SHIPPED. It lives at the project root for editing only; a
generator embeds its contents into the app at release time, the same way
CHANGELOG.md is embedded as the 'What's new' notes. Nothing fetches it at
runtime and the user never sees or edits it.
WRITE FOR LISTENING, NOT READING. This is the one rule that matters here, and
it is why this text is not copied from the user manuals. A listener cannot skim,
cannot re-read, and cannot see where a sentence ends. So:
- One or two sentences. Aim for 15-25 words; 35 is too many.
- Lead with what the control DOES, not with what it is called — the user has
just tapped it, so they can already see its name.
- Say the consequence when there is one worth knowing ('this replaces what is
on this device now'), and leave it out when there isn't.
- Plain words. No jargon, no cross-references, no 'see also'.
- No lists. A spoken list of four options is unfollowable.
KEYS.
tabs         — keyed by the tab's data-tab value.
controls     — keyed by the element's id. Every Settings control has one.
radioGroups  — keyed by the radio group's name attribute.
sections     — keyed by a data-help attribute on a .setting-group whose
heading covers several controls, so tapping the heading
explains the group rather than one control inside it.
COVERAGE IS TESTED. tests/settings-help.test.mjs fails if a control in the
Settings panel has no entry here, or if an entry here matches no control — so a
new setting cannot ship without its spoken help.

tabs.general: Your AI key, where your information is kept, saved copies of your settings, and backing up or moving everything.
tabs.aboutme: The getting-to-know-you questions. Anything you answer here helps the AI suggest responses that sound like you.
tabs.textsize: How big the writing is in each part of the app. Every area is set on its own.
tabs.speech: Your key for the paid services, how the app hears the other person, and the voices used for speaking.
tabs.input: How big the buttons are, how far apart they sit, and where the Express Panel and keyboard go.
tabs.conversation: How the app listens, how many responses it offers you, and what it says while you are choosing.
tabs.practice: Practise a conversation with the AI playing the other person. You do not need a microphone.
tabs.express: Change the buttons on the Express Panel: the phrases you speak, the people you talk to, and how you are feeling.
tabs.controls: Change the words spoken by the command buttons, and your conversation starters and goodbyes.
tabs.keyguard: Spacing settings for fitting a physical keyguard, and a file listing where every button sits.
tabs.about: Which version you are running, what you have spent, and a way to restart the app.
tabs.troubleshooting: Tell us when something goes wrong, and read back what the app has recorded about how it is working.

sections.apiKey: Your key from Anthropic. It is what lets the app suggest responses. Everything else still works without one.
sections.dataFolder: The folder where your answers, your people, and your saved conversations are kept.
sections.settingsProfiles: A saved copy of all your settings. With one saved you can put everything back after a reset, or set up another machine quickly.
sections.backupTransfer: Puts everything about you into a single file, to keep somewhere safe or to move to another device.
sections.deepgramKey: One key for two paid extras: better hearing of the other person, and a much better speaking voice.
sections.yourVoice: The voice that speaks as you.
sections.practicePartnerVoice: The voice used for the other person when you practise, so you can tell it apart from your own.
sections.appUpdates: The app updates itself when a new version is ready. This is here for when you want it to check straight away.
sections.errorLog: A record of anything that has gone wrong. It is what to send if you report a problem.
sections.apiCost: A rough estimate of what you have spent with the AI since the date shown.
sections.reportProblem: Write what went wrong in your own words, then save or copy it. Everything technical is attached for you.
sections.usageSummary: A plain summary of how much you have used the app, how often a suggestion fitted, and how long people waited.
sections.systemInfo: Details about your device and settings, gathered for a problem report. Your keys are never included.
sections.weeklyReports: A short report sent back to us about once a week, so we can see how the app is holding up without asking you.

radioGroups.sttProvider: Who turns the other person's speech into words. Your browser does it free. Deepgram is paid, and works where the browser cannot.
radioGroups.ttsProvider: Which voice speaks for you. This device's own voices are free. A Deepgram voice is paid and usually sounds far better.
radioGroups.keyboardMode: Whether you type on a keyboard you plug in, or on the app's own keyboard on the screen.
radioGroups.keyboardDock: Whether the Express Panel and keyboard sit along the bottom of the screen, or down one side.
radioGroups.expressTapMode: Whether one tap speaks an Express Panel button, or two are needed so you cannot set it off by accident.

controls.apiKeyInput: Paste your Anthropic key here. It stays on this device and is never put into a backup.
controls.pasteApiKeyBtn: Pastes a key you have already copied, so you do not have to type it out.
controls.testApiKeyBtn: Checks your key with Anthropic and tells you whether it was accepted. It costs nothing.
controls.pickFolderBtn: Choose the folder where your information is kept. Choose the same one each time you set the app up again.
controls.makeStorageDurableBtn: Asks the browser not to throw your information away if it starts running short of room.
controls.settingsProfileSelect: Choose one of your saved settings profiles, ready to load or delete.
controls.loadSettingsProfileBtn: Puts every setting from the chosen profile back in place. The app restarts to do it.
controls.updateSettingsProfileBtn: Saves your settings as they are now over the profile you are using. Do this after any change you want to keep.
controls.deleteSettingsProfileBtn: Removes the chosen profile. Your current settings are left exactly as they are.
controls.settingsProfileNameInput: A name for a new profile. Naming it after the device helps if you use more than one.
controls.saveSettingsProfileBtn: Saves all your settings as they are now, as a new profile under the name you typed.
controls.exportDataBtn: Saves everything about you into one file: your answers, your people, your buttons and your conversations.
controls.importDataBtn: Loads everything back from a backup file you choose. This replaces what is on this device now.
controls.importDataFile: Choose the backup file you want to load.
controls.backupFileSelect: Choose one of the backups the app has already made for you.
controls.restoreBackupBtn: Puts everything back from the backup you chose. This replaces what is on this device now.
controls.responseFontSelect: How big the writing is on the suggested response cards.
controls.transcriptFontSelect: How big the writing is in the conversation, where what was said is shown.
controls.composerFontSelect: How big the writing is when you type something in your own words.
controls.expressFontSelect: How big the writing is on the Express Panel buttons.
controls.deepgramKeyInput: Paste your Deepgram key here. It stays on this device and is never put into a backup.
controls.pasteDeepgramKeyBtn: Pastes a Deepgram key you have already copied.
controls.testDeepgramKeyBtn: Checks your Deepgram key and tells you whether it was accepted.
controls.voiceSelect: Choose which of this device's voices speaks as you.
controls.showNoveltyVoicesInput: Shows the joke voices built into this device, like the robot and cartoon ones. They are hidden to begin with.
controls.testVoiceBtn: Says a few words so you can hear the voice before you settle on it.
controls.auraVoiceSelect: Choose which Deepgram voice speaks as you.
controls.testAuraVoiceBtn: Says a few words in the Deepgram voice you have chosen.
controls.partnerVoiceSelect: Choose the voice for the person you practise with. Automatic picks one that is not yours.
controls.testPartnerVoiceBtn: Says a few words in the practice partner's voice.
controls.auraPartnerVoiceSelect: Choose the Deepgram voice for the person you practise with.
controls.testAuraPartnerVoiceBtn: Says a few words in the practice partner's Deepgram voice.
controls.buttonSizeSlider: How big the buttons are. Bigger ones are easier to hit, but fewer of them fit on the screen.
controls.buttonGapSlider: The space between the buttons. On a keyguard this is the width of the bars between the holes.
controls.minGapSlider: The smallest space allowed between buttons, however big you make them.
controls.resetSizingBtn: Puts button size and spacing back to how they started. Screen edge margin is left alone.
controls.sideDockPositionToggle: Which side the Express Panel and keyboard sit on, the left or the right.
controls.bottomLayoutSelect: How the Express Panel and keyboard are laid out when they sit along the bottom.
controls.sideLayoutSelect: How the Express Panel and keyboard are laid out when they sit down one side.
controls.noSaveDefaultInput: Begin every conversation without saving it. You can still change your mind for one conversation at a time.
controls.responsesPerCategoryInput: Whether you are offered four suggested responses, or eight.
controls.choiceChipMaxInput: How many of the other person's choices can appear as buttons on your Express Panel.
controls.silenceThresholdInput: How long the other person has to pause before the app asks the AI for suggestions. Zero means as soon as it hears them stop.
controls.autoRelistenInput: Start listening again on its own after you speak, so you need not press Listen every time.
controls.listenChimeInput: Play a short tone when listening begins, so the other person knows the app is listening.
controls.initialDelayInput: How long the app waits before saying something to hold your place while you choose.
controls.subsequentDelayInput: How long before it says another one, if you are still choosing.
controls.maxPlaceholdersInput: How many of those holding phrases it may say in one turn. Set it to none if you would rather it stayed quiet.
controls.doubleTapMsSelect: How quickly the two taps have to follow one another to count as a double tap.
controls.appMarginSlider: Moves the whole app in from the edges of the screen, so a keyguard fits inside a tight case opening.
controls.dockSepSlider: The gap between the keyboard area and the rest of the screen. It does not move the keyboard itself.
controls.transcriptSepSlider: The gap between the conversation and the row of command buttons underneath it.
controls.titleBarHeightInput: The height of the window bar above the app, so the keyguard file lines up with a screenshot.
controls.generateOpeningsBtn: Writes a file saying exactly where every button sits, for cutting a keyguard.
controls.reloadAppBtn: Fetches the newest version and starts the app again. Nothing you have saved is lost.
controls.errorLogView: A record of anything that has gone wrong, the most recent first.
controls.copyErrorLogBtn: Copies the errors, along with the conversations they happened in, ready to paste into a message.
controls.clearErrorLogBtn: Empties this list. The copy kept in your data folder is left alone.
controls.resetUsageBtn: Sets the cost estimate back to zero and starts counting again from today.
controls.fullscreenInput: Expands the app to fill the whole screen, hiding the title bar. Turn it off to get the title bar back, or maximise the window instead.
controls.problemNoteInput: Describe what went wrong. One line is plenty. Say what you did and what happened instead.
controls.saveProblemReportBtn: Saves the whole report as a file you can send us. Use this one if you are on a tablet.
controls.copyProblemReportBtn: Copies the whole report so you can paste it into a message or an email.
controls.usageSummaryView: A summary built from your saved conversations. Nothing anyone said appears here, only counts and timings.
controls.refreshUsageSummaryBtn: Rebuilds the summary from your saved conversations, including anything since you opened this.
controls.copyUsageSummaryBtn: Copies the usage summary so you can paste it into a message.
controls.systemInfoView: What the app can tell about your device, your screen, and your settings. Neither of your keys is included.
controls.copySystemInfoBtn: Copies the system information so you can paste it into a message.
controls.testerNameInput: The name we gave you when you joined. It lets us tell whose report is whose, so we can get back to you.
controls.weeklySendEnabledInput: Sends a short report about once a week when you open the app. Turn it off if you would rather not; nothing else changes.
controls.weeklyReportContents: Lists exactly what a weekly report contains. Nothing anyone said is ever in one, and neither are your keys.
controls.weeklySendLogView: When reports were sent and how big they were. It does not show what was in them.
